samples.question: This image shows five framed rectangular panels of identical size standing side by side in one row, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Every panel contains exactly six solid dots of the same single colour and the same size, so all five panels carry the same number of dots and the same amount of ink, and colour, dot count and dot size carry no information. Every panel also carries exactly one straight dashed grey line that runs right across it at that panel's own arbitrary tilt; this dashed line is that panel's mirror line, and its tilt and its place inside the panel carry no information. A panel counts as mirror-symmetric when folding it along its own dashed line would lay every one of its six dots exactly onto another of its dots: each dot has a partner on the other side of the dashed line, the two partners stand the same distance from the line, and the line through the two partners meets the dashed line square on. No dot ever sits on the dashed line, and the dots are never mirrored across any other line, only across the dashed line drawn in their own panel. In exactly one panel all six dots are mirror-symmetric about that panel's dashed line. In each of the other four panels exactly one single dot has been pushed off its mirror place, by at least 12 pixels, which is more than three quarters of a dot's width, while the remaining dots there still mirror one another. Only the dot centres and the dashed line matter, and no partner pairs are drawn. Which numbered panel has all six of its dots mirror-symmetric about its own dashed line? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.
